title: C# Questions & Answers - Comparison of Strings
sourceFile: Strings Comparison - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on comparison of two strings in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of these methods of the String class is used to compare two String objects for equality?
questions.explanation: In C#, methods use PascalCase. The correct method to check string equality is 'Equals()'.

questions.question: Which of these methods is used to compare two strings and returns an integer (0, 1, or -1) representing their relative sort order?
questions.explanation: The static Compare() method returns: 0 if strings are equal, a positive integer if the first string is 'greater' in sort order, and a negative integer if it is 'lesser'.

questions.question: Which of these methods of the String class is used to check whether a substring exists at the beginning of a string?
questions.explanation: The StartsWith() method determines whether the beginning of a string instance matches a specified string.

questions.question: Which method returns a new string where a specified number of characters have been deleted from a specific position?
questions.explanation: The 'Remove(int startIndex, int count)' method is the one that deletes a specific number of characters starting from a specified position.

questions.question: What is the value returned by the CompareTo() function if the invoking string is less than the string compared?
questions.explanation: CompareTo() returns 0 if strings are equal, a negative value (less than zero) if the instance is less than the value, and a positive value if it is greater.
